title: test: cover sparse receipts and resolver errors through the picker CLI
body:
## Change and scope

This adds three real-CLI integration tests for two acceptance paths missing from PR #5761: sparse-reference receipt metadata, and a current-resolver error after the legacy child has succeeded. Production scripts, catalogue and selected record are unchanged.

**Dependency and exact increment.** This is stacked on Ali Romman's fixture repair, PR #5761 at `ba8a9e640e1983f3c29993fefa3f46e8ed03313a`. Its three files are included unchanged. The [new increment](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/compare/ba8a9e640e1983f3c29993fefa3f46e8ed03313a...ebda0dbcd10cc2c2aec73d6a36d3a5e70278ca9d) is exactly one 100-line file, `tests/test_research_current_assignment_cli.py`. Merge order and independent acceptance remain maintainer decisions; no merge is requested.

## Task and overlap

Task `portable-replay` has `scope_status=changed`: this replaces the historical gzip-comparison premise with a confirmed revision-8 CLI acceptance-coverage gap. It prevents silent loss of reference-validation receipts or false success without changing scientific routing.

The tests use the predecessor's exact frozen cards, real CLI subprocesses and owned temporary Git repositories. They check both materialized routes; unchanged HEAD + skip-worktree omissions at the wrapper CLI, including preservation of existing catalogue omissions; and child status 0 followed by wrapper status 2, empty stdout and the targeted diagnostic when the current helper is absent. Reference files in these fixtures are inert: no historical scientific command runs.

## Validation

Validation on CPython 3.12.14:

| Implementation in isolated audit copy | Unchanged 12 predecessor tests | With 3 new tests, normal / optimized |
|---|---|---|
| Correct source | PASS | 15 PASS / 15 PASS |
| CLI `if omitted:` changed to `if False:` | PASS | 2 intended sparse-receipt assertion failures / same |
| Resolver exception handler `return 2` changed to `return 0` | PASS | 1 intended status assertion failure / same |

These are deliberately injected faults, not defects claimed in the production implementation. Both mutations are applied separately and leave the existing tests/fixtures byte-identical. An initial incomplete path-only audit fixture failed before the mutation comparison; that setup attempt was retained and corrected, not counted as a result. A separate Git-free exported harness passed all 15 tests with immutable source bytes. Its catalogue reference placeholders validate CLI paths only.

Reproduce the correct-source checks:

```sh
python3.12 -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_current_assignment*.py' -v
PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 python3.12 -I -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_current_assignment*.py' -v
```

The second command also optimizes CLI children through `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1`. New file SHA256: `f6e43ca46d470a476bd1b6689fc30edeb87d1289632c82713147c16d6ad0f8bc`; publication head `ebda0dbcd10cc2c2aec73d6a36d3a5e70278ca9d`.

Canonical main was fetched again at 20:00 UTC: `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. Open-PR overlap and [canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5758#discussioncomment-19203583) distinguish this audit from the predecessor repair. Earlier broad coverage included 351 open records; Discussion coverage is partial and unpublished work remains unknown. The sparse selected-input preflight reported omitted inputs; no full selected-source baseline, native replay, supplier admission, kappa improvement or frontier change is claimed.

## Credit

Credit Ali Romman for PR #5761's repair and fixtures, and Douglas Colkitt, Mihir Srivastava and retained routing authors. New tests/audit by ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; separate implementation and read-only review contexts were used. Apache-2.0. Maintainer edits disabled.

## Open next questions

Independently review the two mutation witnesses and the one-file increment, then resolve the dependency on #5761 through normal maintainer review. No further generic mutation expansion is justified by this result.
